additional_info.subject: ID0399052-DC/Si-D/DK[Xdc81P] - FC16 tripped CRM:00315002241
additional_info.body:
Dear Rasmus Eksten,
Thank you for reaching
out
to eMobility Support. My name is
Francisco
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset
:
MP / S3 170003386
ChargerID/Serial No.
:
Xdc81P
Problem Description
: FC16 is tripping randomly during start charge
Troubleshooting
:
I will share with you the tests with did today with Simen from RC-NO, for now, it would be best to wait for the result of the FC16 result (please check below).
The problem seems to be related to the Contactor or the Fuse itself.
What we tested was, removing the cables from the XD441 and XD442:
QA09 - XD441:8C
QA10 - XD442:14C
QA11 - XD441:10C
QA12 - XD442:16C
All of them showed around 300-400kOhm which is correct with our values in TC.
We checked XD9.1B/A, removed and plugged back in → no issues it seems
Checked XD12.1 and also all properly attached.
We changed FC16 with FC17 to see if there is any problem with FC16.
If we have an error in FC16 (which is now in FC17), then we have a faulty fuse
If we have an error in the new FC16 (FC17), then it means we still have a problem in the circuit.
Please let me know your feedback if you want to send someone on-site to check this or if you want to wait for the news.
For future reference, your case number is
0399052
, please do refer to this in all further communication regarding this issue.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Francisco de Matos Joaquim

additional_info.subject: ID0399052-DC/Si-D/DK[Xdc81P] - FC16 tripped CRM:00315002241
additional_info.body:
Hi Rasmus, good morning. I hope you had a nice weekend.
Unfortunately, the problem happened this morning with charger Xdc81P:
It seems that someone started the update, that's good, let's update to v6.0.3 and get the error again. Hopefully there is no need to go to site but from my perspective, it's impossible that the SPD is faulty since the SPD when it goes to Error, it should never come back and needs to be replaced. Here we see that the SPD comes back after the error during a reboot or similar, so I would assume there is something similar to this one I found previously:
If you have time to check it on-site or if there is any trained technician that can check this connection if it's damaged or just plug out and plug back in to see if it was indeed loose.
I will wait for your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco
